faq: What does this tool calculate?
Pace per kilometre from pace per mile: min/mile ÷ 1.609344, shown as minutes and seconds per kilometre.
Is the calculation done locally?
Yes — instantly in your browser, nothing uploaded.
How accurate is the result?
Exact to the mile's definition; only the final rounding to seconds approximates, and visibly.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. This converts the pace you ran or plan to run; traffic is not a runner's unit problem.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Courses are measured along their paths — which is why your converted pace matches the course's markers: both follow the road, not the crow.
Why divide and not multiply?
A kilometre is 0.621371 of a mile, so it takes 0.621371 times as long to cover at the same speed. The pace number shrinks with the unit.
The reverse direction?
Multiply by 1.609344 — the Minutes per KM to Minutes per Mile Converter handles it.
What is a 15:00/mile hike in km?
9:19/km — hiking paces convert identically; the trail speaks both dialects.
Why does the km pace look so much faster?
It is the same speed over a shorter unit. The flattery is the unit's, and everyone in metric countries lives with it.
Rounding over a long race?
Seconds are rounded per split; over 42 splits the drift stays inside a couple of seconds — far below pacing error.
